title: The abelian category of coefficient towers
statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite and $T$ a scheme.

1. $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ is the category of
   $\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^\bullet$-modules in the topos of inverse systems
   (functors $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}\to$ sheaves) on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$
   (compare Bhatt–Scholze, Section 3.5). It is a Grothendieck abelian category
   in which kernels, cokernels and filtered colimits are computed level by
   level; we use its ordinary derived category $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$.
2. Evaluation at level $n$, $C_\bullet\mapsto C_n$, is an exact functor
   $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)\to\Mod(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n)$; for
   $C_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ we write $C_n$ for its image
   in $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)$.
3. The transition maps induce, for $m\leq n$, *reduction maps*
   $$
   C_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n}\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^m\longrightarrow C_m
   \quad\text{in }D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^m),
   $$
   natural in $C_\bullet$ and compatible with composition $m'\leq m\leq n$.

proof.text: Explicitly curry the recorded varying-coefficient product-site module presheaves into StrictRingSystem. Vertical slices retain the original section modules and restrictions; horizontal arrows give the semilinear transitions. Conversely compose horizontal transitions and vertical restrictions. Product functoriality and the strict identity/composition laws prove the two functors and their identity-component unit and counit. Equality of the forgotten commutative coefficient diagram with spCoefficientRings gives the sectionwise normalized equivalence. The previously proved abelian-axioms theorem uses the vertical topology and its sheaf criterion to rebundle the same module presheaves as module sheaves.

proof.text: Apply systemLevelLeftExtensionTheory to the explicit commutative ring diagram. Transfer its Grothendieck structure across the normalized equivalence. The equivalence preserves finite limits and colimits; preservation of binary products and zero morphisms implies additivity. The existing strict-system evaluation instances therefore give exact evaluation. The theory supplies evaluation coproducts; together with finite colimits these imply preservation of all small colimits, including the required filtered colimits. proof.text: Prove compatibility of derived scalar comparisons on arbitrary source-level complexes by resolving that source once with a K-flat complex with flat terms. The independent-coefficient tensor comparison identifies flatness with the predicate used by SystemTensorCoherence. Naturality carries the comparisons along the quasi-isomorphism; its localization and derived-tensor images are isomorphisms and can be cancelled. On the resolution use the stipulated normalized derived unitor/associator computations and ordinary reduction coherence. Finally use localization faithfulness and naturality of evaluation comparison isomorphisms to obtain reduction_identity and reduction_comp on every derived tower. No simultaneous tower resolution or separate preservation-of-K-flatness argument is required.
